title: automate-kms-hsm-tls-rotation-private-installer-helm-terraform
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Automates TLS certificate rotation and KMS/HSM key integration for the private installer. Adds Helm chart hooks and Terraform module updates to support scheduled rotations, Vault and sealed-secrets re-encryption, and safe rollbacks.
description:
Background: Customers running Redwood Private have asked for automated secrets and certificate lifecycle management in private/on-prem installs (Vault, KMS/HSM, sealed-secrets). Currently operators must manually coordinate KMS key re-creation, TLS cert rotation across load-balancers, and sealed-secrets re-seal steps during maintenance windows. This PR provides an end-to-end automation path that integrates the private-installer, Helm charts, and Terraform modules to support scheduled and manual rotation workflows while preserving rollback safety and auditability.

What this changes:
- Adds a new terraform module (modules/kms_rotation) that can provision rotation schedules and Cloud HSM key aliases, and emits rotation signals to the installer control-plane.
- Extends the private-installer control plane to support rotation jobs (controller/rotation) that orchestrate: KMS/HSM key versioning, Kubernetes TLS secret rollout, sealed-secrets re-encryption, and Vault re-seal/unseal steps.
- Helm chart updates (charts/private-installer) include pre/post hooks for safe pod restarts, a new RotationConfig CRD, and templated Job manifests for re-encrypting sealed-secrets and reloading KMS creds.
- Adds a temporary compatibility layer so installs using sealed-secrets or Vault can opt-in to rotation automation via installer config (values.yaml) without breaking existing clusters.
- Adds a set of e2e scenarios in perf-canary to validate zero-downtime certificate rotation under load and validate KV cache persistence across rotation.

Design and safety goals:
- Safe by default: rotation is opt-in and requires explicit RotationConfig in operator's installer values.
- Rollbackable: artifacts (previous TLS certs, KMS key versions) are preserved until rotation completes successfully; the controller supports a revert path.
- Auditability: all rotation events are recorded with request IDs and surfaced to the console/observability stack.
- Vendor-agnostic: supports Vault (auto-unseal), sealed-secrets, and KMS/HSM providers via modular provider adapters.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module for rotation schedules + variables and examples.
- [x] Installer controller for rotation orchestration with revert path.
- [x] Helm chart hooks and CRD templates.
- [x] Docs: installer/README and upgrade notes.
- [x] E2E tests in perf-canary validating downtime and key continuity.
- [x] Integration tests for Vault and sealed-secrets re-encryption.

Upgrade notes / operator actions:
- Operators who want automated rotation must add a RotationConfig to their installer values and set the provider block (vault|sealed_secrets|kms_hsm).
- For KMS/HSM providers, ensure the terraform module has permission to create key aliases and rotation schedules in the target account/HSM.
- The first rotation run will create a new key version/cert and perform staged rollout of Secrets across deployments. Follow the console logs under the "Rotations" dashboard for progress.

Related: Linear ENG-4782, SEC-304, OPS-912. Jira SUP-2217 captures customer support context.

Why now: This reduces manual steps and support burden for enterprise customers on private deployments and enables security teams to enforce regular key/cert rotation with automation aligned to their config management pipelines.
